item.text: {"reviews":[{"benchmark":"arc","instrument_review":"MESA supports interpreting ARC-AGI-2 scores as performance on unfamiliar grid puzzles under specified conditions. Development checks, scoring tests and evaluation policies are documented. Repeated-run variation, uncertainty in comparisons and transfer to broader reasoning remain unresolved. Partial problem credit also requires care when describing problems as solved.","supported_claims":["The benchmark tests inference of grid transformations from examples.","Official software averages per-problem fractions of correctly completed inputs, allowing two attempts per input.","Human testing informed puzzle selection and matching test-set difficulty for people.","Public marking tests examine several correct and incorrect output cases."],"documented_problems":["Verified evaluations use one run, leaving repeated-run variation unmeasured in those evaluations.","The software's partial problem credit differs from the dataset's definition of a fully solved problem.","The change record documents corrected squares and unclear examples without recalculating every affected AI score."],"missing_information":["Repeated-run score variation and uncertainty estimates for AI comparisons.","Systematic tests of instruction, presentation and software changes.","Evidence linking grid scores to language, social interaction or real-world work.","Evidence that matching human difficulty also makes test sets equivalent for AI systems."],"reinterpretations":["Reasoning is operationalized as inferring and completing two-dimensional grid transformations.","A reported score measures exact output success under permitted attempts; it does not establish the reasoning process used.","Matching test sets for human difficulty does not establish equivalent difficulty for AI systems."],"closing_note":"The questionnaire distinguishes testing from favourable findings; limited coverage does not negate documented testing. References to solved problems should distinguish full completion from partial problem credit.","mesa_answers":[{"id":1,"choice":"Yes"},{"id":2,"choice":"Yes"},{"id":3,"choice":"Yes"},{"id":4,"choice":"Yes"},{"id":5,"choice":"Yes"},{"id":6,"choice":"Yes"},{"id":7,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Human testing and rule review justify selection, but broader reasoning coverage remains limited."},{"id":8,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Developer review and documented corrections show checking occurred."},{"id":9,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Grid puzzles cover some rule inference, without establishing coverage of broader intelligence."},{"id":10,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Exact matches reward successful transformations, but do not establish the reasoning used."},{"id":11,"choice":"Partly","comment":"The averaging rule is clear, but its interpretation as a broader ability measure lacks support."},{"id":12,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Public tests check correct answers, dimensions, changed squares and missing outputs."},{"id":13,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Human results inform difficulty, but cover a larger pool and do not establish equivalent AI conditions."},{"id":14,"choice":"No","comment":"The specified verified-testing policy uses one run; other routes remain unclear."},{"id":15,"choice":"Not sure"},{"id":16,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"Score-variation estimates or ranges are not supplied."},{"id":17,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Developers examined repeated rules and designed puzzles to resist program-search shortcuts."},{"id":18,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Exposure monitoring and hidden-data protections are described, but exposure remains possible."},{"id":19,"choice":"Yes","comment":"Policies distinguish development from evaluation and restrict feedback-driven repeated improvement."},{"id":20,"choice":"Not sure"},{"id":21,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Verified settings are recorded, but other routes differ and human difficulty matching does not establish AI equivalence."},{"id":22,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Public problems, software and tests support inspection; hidden materials remain controlled."},{"id":23,"choice":"Yes"},{"id":24,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Dated corrections are recorded, but effects on all affected scores are not established."},{"id":25,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Grid-performance claims are supported; connections to broader intelligence remain unresolved."}]},{"benchmark":"designqa","instrument_review":"MESA supports using DesignQA to examine performance on its specified engineering-document tasks and information conditions. Practical materials and setup experiments support this narrow interpretation. Uneven task coverage, wording-sensitive marking and differing information supplies limit broader comparisons. Transfer to other documents and fine distinctions between systems remain unsupported.","supported_claims":["The benchmark contains 1,451 question-answer pairs across six engineering task groups.","Tasks use actual competition rules, vehicle materials and test data.","Some question review and marking tests occurred.","Experiments examined changes to passages, labels, scale bars and highlighted images.","The paper acknowledges uncertainty about performance on other technical documents."],"documented_problems":["Task groups are highly uneven, ranging from 1,192 individual-rule questions to 16 performance questions.","Wording and formatting can affect credit, including missing commas and valid rules absent from references.","Systems receive different information supplies, including whole rulebooks or retrieved passages.","All described scale-bar drawings comply, allowing an always-yes answer to earn decision credit on that portion.","One released answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding question count in the paper.","Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every reported result."],"missing_information":["Complete evidence of marking accuracy and consistency.","Repeated testing under identical conditions and sufficient uncertainty estimates for close comparisons.","A human-engineer baseline.","Systematic prior-exposure checks and clear training and repeated-submission policies.","Evidence supporting transfer to other standards or real engineering projects.","Complete reuse rules and explanations of how revisions affect scores."],"reinterpretations":["Engineering-document understanding is operationalized through six task groups using one competition rulebook.","Scores reflect the AI together with its supplied or retrieved information.","Text-similarity credit can reflect wording and formatting as well as engineering understanding.","Variation across changed passage sets measures setup sensitivity rather than repetition under identical conditions."],"closing_note":"No material instruction ambiguity prevents review. systematic overlap checks and a protected set are not established."},{"id":19,"choice":"Not sure"},{"id":20,"choice":"Not sure"},{"id":21,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Information differences are disclosed, but they limit comparisons of AI systems themselves."},{"id":22,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Public materials support inspection but do not completely reproduce every historical result."},{"id":23,"choice":"Not sure","comment":"A licence file and complete responsible-reuse rules were not found in the reviewed sources."},{"id":24,"choice":"Partly","comment":"Code history identifies revisions without clearly explaining score effects."},{"id":25,"choice":"Yes","comment":"The supplied account reports explicit limits on generalization and acknowledges imperfect marking."}]}]}
